overview: Self-Harmony is a test-time reinforcement learning framework that uses a single model in dual roles (Solver and Reframer) to generate reliable pseudo-labels via harmonic mean consensus across original and paraphrased question views, replacing majority voting to avoid amplifying spurious answers.

modules.name: Configuration & Experiment Management
modules.description: Manages experiment configurations including model selection, dataset paths, hyperparameters (learning rate, rollout counts, reward coefficients, KL loss settings), and experiment tracking integration for reproducible runs across all model-dataset combinations.

modules.name: Dataset Loading & Preprocessing
modules.description: Loads and preprocesses multiple reasoning benchmarks (MATH500, GSM8K, AIME, AMC, GPQA, MMLU-Pro), handling dataset-specific formatting, question extraction, and batch construction for fully unsupervised training where ground-truth labels are never exposed to the training pipeline.

modules.name: Prompt Engineering Module
modules.description: Implements the Solver and Reframer prompt templates. The Solver prompt elicits step-by-step reasoning with boxed final answers. The Reframer prompt instructs the model to first transform the problem using a chosen strategy (Concretize, Generalize, Domain Shift, Add Noise, Reverse, Incremental Complexity, Focus on Constraints, POV Shift) and then solve the transformed version within a single generation.

modules.name: Rollout Generation Engine
modules.description: Generates multiple rollout trajectories for both original questions (via the Solver) and reframed questions (via the fused Reframer-Solver action), managing sampling parameters (temperature, top-p, top-k) and producing structured output containing the transformation, solution, and final answer for each rollout.

modules.name: Answer Extraction & Rule Verification
modules.description: Extracts final answers from rollout text by parsing boxed outputs, and applies dataset-specific rule-based verifiers (math verifiers for MATH/GSM/AIME/AMC, specialized verifiers for GPQA/MMLU-Pro) to determine answer correctness against pseudo-labels.

modules.name: Harmonic Mean Score Pseudo-Label Selector
modules.description: Implements the core pseudo-label selection mechanism: computes empirical answer frequencies from original (p_hat_0) and reframed (p_hat_1) rollouts, then selects the answer maximizing the harmonic mean score 2*p_hat_0(a)*p_hat_1(a)/(p_hat_0(a)+p_hat_1(a)), naturally favoring view-consistent answers and penalizing view-dependent spurious solutions.

modules.name: Baseline Pseudo-Label Selectors
modules.description: Implements alternative pseudo-label selection strategies for comparison: single-view majority voting, dual-view majority voting (sum of probabilities), cross selection (branches swap outputs), and Co-Reward-style contrastive agreement, enabling fair benchmarking under identical computational budgets.

modules.name: Reward Computation Module
modules.description: Computes rewards for both the initial solving action (binary correctness against pseudo-label) and the fused reframing-and-solving action. The fused reward uses a multiplicative design where correctness acts as a success gate, modulated by a format penalty (structural violations) and a diversity penalty (Jensen-Shannon divergence between original and reframed answer distributions), ensuring only correct answers with well-formed and meaningfully different reframings receive positive reward.

modules.name: GRPO Policy Optimization
modules.description: Implements Group Relative Policy Optimization for updating the shared Solver-Reframer model, incorporating KL divergence regularization against the reference policy, gradient clipping, PPO-style clip ratios, and micro-batch accumulation for stable training across varying batch sizes per dataset.

modules.name: Self-Harmony Training Loop Controller
modules.description: Orchestrates the full training workflow: for each minibatch, (1) generate Solver rollouts for original questions, (2) generate fused Reframer-Solver rollouts producing paraphrased questions and their solutions, (3) compute harmonic mean pseudo-labels, (4) compute rewards for both action types, (5) aggregate gradients from both GRPO objectives and update the shared model. Manages epoch progression, validation checkpoints, and early stopping.

modules.name: Evaluation Metrics Suite
modules.description: Computes all evaluation metrics: Pass@1 accuracy (average over multiple rollouts), pseudo-label accuracy, F1 score, and Spearman correlation between predicted and true correctness, across both overall benchmarks and difficulty-stratified subsets (L1-L5 for MATH).

modules.name: Ablation Study Framework
modules.description: Supports controlled ablation experiments by toggling individual framework components: removing the format reward, removing the diversity reward, replacing HMS with majority voting, replacing HMS with cross selection, and replacing the multiplicative reward with an additive alternative, enabling systematic attribution of performance to each design choice.

modules.name: Sensitivity Analysis & Hyperparameter Search
modules.description: Performs grid search over the format reward coefficient and diversity reward coefficient, recording performance across the full parameter space to demonstrate robustness. Also analyzes sensitivity to the number of rollouts and the Infomax penalty weight lambda mapping to generalized means.

modules.name: Semantic Consistency Validation
modules.description: Validates that the Reframer preserves semantic equivalence by comparing external oracle model (GPT-4o, Claude) answers on original vs. reframed questions, computing consistency rates. Also performs stress tests with varying Reframer scales to assess robustness to imperfect paraphrasing quality.

modules.name: Inference-Only Harmonic Mean Selector
modules.description: Evaluates the harmonic mean as a plug-and-play pseudo-label selector at test time without any parameter updates, sweeping rollout budgets and comparing against majority voting across confidence-correctness quadrants to demonstrate scalability and standalone utility.

modules.name: Generalized Mean Comparison & Result Reporting
modules.description: Compares different generalized mean selectors (arithmetic, geometric, harmonic, quadratic) mapped to varying lambda penalties in the view-invariant Infomax objective, analyzes performance across confidence-correctness quadrants, and generates result tables, heatmaps, and training curves for publication-quality reporting.
